summary: Michael Oppitz is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987-1988) and the University of Zurich (~1990-2008).

Michael Puett works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1986-1994) under Anthony C. Yu, and became John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Humanities at Harvard University (~1994).

Michael Pye is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology scholar who studied under Maurice Wiles. He held posts at the University of Leeds (~1970-1978) and served as Professor at Lancaster University (~1991-1995).

Michael Radich specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard (~2001-2007) under Robert M. Gimello and studied at Kyoto University (2009). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (~2005-2017) and Heidelberg University (~2018).
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, where he was dictionary editor (attested 1981), held a post in 1992, and served as a collaborator (attested 2008).

Michael Sheehy works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at CIIS (attested 2007) under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2006) and held positions at Pittsburgh, MPIWG, Leipzig University, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991) and served as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.
Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1838-1847) and later held a post there (~1878-1902).

Michael W. Meister specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1964-1968) and Harvard University (~1969-1974), and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1976).

Michael Witzel works in Indology and linguistics, having studied under Paul Thieme (~1965-1971). He served as Director at the Nepal Research Centre (~1972-1977) and held Chairs of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978-1986) and Harvard University (1987).

Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, where he later served as Director (attested 2009-2015). He also held posts at Stanford, Nepal Research Centre, and Nyingma Institute.
Michael von Brück is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology scholar. He held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1988-1991) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1991-2014).

Michaela Haas specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Bonn under the supervision of Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Jigme Namgyal and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and completed her PhD at LMU Munich (-2014), later holding posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Göttingen, and Stanford University (attested 2017).

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at ENS (~1852-1855) and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at Collège de France (1866-1905) and director at EPHE (~1868-1882).

Michel Clasquin is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He completed his studies and doctoral thesis at the University of South Africa between 1991 and 1999, and held a post there in 1990.

Michel Mohr specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. After earning his PhD at the University of Geneva (post 1987-1992), he held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2000-2006) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2008-2012).

Michel Strickmann specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at EPHE and Paris Diderot University, and held academic posts at UC Berkeley (1978), the University of Bordeaux (~1978-1980), and the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (1983-1985).
